ORAL JUDGMENT (PER: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE ASHOK S. KINAGI) These appeals are filed by the Divisional Controller, KSRTC1 challenging the common judgment and award dated 17.03.2020 passed in MVC Nos.1582, 1583 and 1584 of 2015.

2. Brief facts leading rise to the filing of these appeals are as follows:
2.1.
On 03.05.2015, the petitioners were travelling by a car bearing Reg.No.KA-27/A-7282 from Harihar to Harapanahalli through state highway road.

When the car came near Telagi Village of Harapahanalli Taluk, a KSRTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-18/F-0581 came from the hind side driven by its driver in rash and negligent manner with a high speed, and dashed to the car and caused an accident.
As a result, the petitioners have sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

Hence,
the petitioners filed claim petitions under Section 166 of the Motor Karnataka State Road Transport Corporation NC: 2026:KHC-D:3638 HC-KAR Vehicles Act, 1988,
seeking compensations on account of the injuries sustained in the road traffic accident.

sentences.text:
Accordingly, prays to allow the claim petition.
2.2.

Hence, prays to dismiss the claim petitions.
2.3.
The claim petitions were clubbed together and common issues were framed by the Tribunal.

2.4. To substantiate their cases, the petitioners in MVC Nos. 1582 and 1583 of 2015 examined themselves as PW1 and PW2, the minor petitioner in MVC No. 1584 of 2015 examined his next friend father as PW3, the petitioners also examined the Doctor as PW4, and marked NC:
2026:KHC-D:3638 HC-KAR 21 documents as Exs.P1 to P21.

In rebuttal, the KSRTC examined the Conductor of the bus as RW1 and marked 1 document as Ex.R1.
2.5.

The Tribunal, after assessing the verbal and documentary evidence, allowed the claim petitions in part vide judgment dated 17.03.2020 with costs and awarded compensations of 1,69,900/- to the petitioner in MVC No. 1582 of 2015, 2,06,400/- in MVC No. 1583 of 2015 and 1,20,000/- to the minor petitioner in MVC No. 1584 of 2015 with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petitions till their realisation, and directed the KSRTC to deposit the compensation amounts.
3. The KSRTC, aggrieved by the impugned common judgment and award, filed these appeals.

4. Heard the arguments of learned counsel for the KSRTC and learned counsel for the petitioners.
5. Learned counsel for the KSRTC submits that, the compensations awarded by the Tribunal are on the NC: 2026:KHC-D:3638 HC-KAR higher side.
He submits that, the petitioners have examined the Doctor as PW4, who is not a treated doctor and the disability assessed by the Tribunal is on the higher side.
Hence, on these grounds, he prays to allow the appeals.
6. Per contra, learned counsel for the petitioners submits that, the compensation amounts awarded by the Tribunal are on the lower side.

He submits that, the petitioners have examined the Doctor as PW4, who has opined that the petitioners have suffered permanent disabilities and issued the disability certificates marked as Exs.P6, P10 and P18.
The Tribunal, considering the disability certificates issued by PW4, has rightly awarded the compensations.
Hence, on these grounds, he prays to dismiss the appeals.

7. Perused the records and considered the submissions of the learned counsel for the parties.
NC: 2026:KHC-D:3638 HC-KAR 8.
It is undisputed that the accident had occurred due to a rash and negligent driving of the driver of the KSRTC bus.
A charge sheet is filed against the driver of the bus and the petitioners have produced the same marked as Ex.P17.
The Tribunal, relying upon Ex.P17 has rightly held that the accident had occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending bus.

The petitioner has produced the wound certificate which discloses that he has sustained 3 injuries in the accident and out of those injuries, injury No.1 is simple and injury Nos.2 and 3 are grievous in nature.

As per Ex.P6 i.e., the disability certificate issued by PW4, who has opined that he has examined the petitioner clinically and radiologically and issued the disability certificate at Ex.P6,
wherein the petitioner has sustained fracture of lower end of the radius and ulna bone and fracture of 6th, NC: 2026:KHC-D:3638 HC-KAR 7th and 8th ribs on the right side.
PW4 has assessed the disability to the extent of 35% to the whole body, wherein the Tribunal has assessed the disability to the extent of 8.75% to the whole body.
The disability assessed by the Tribunal is just and proper.
The petitioner contended that, he was aged about 45 years as of the date of the accident, and was doing agricultural and vegetable business and used to earn 15,000/- per month.

The petitioner, however,
to substantiate the income the petitioner, he has not produced any income proof, wherein the Tribunal has assessed the notional income at 7,000/- per month.

In the absence of the income proof, the Tribunal ought to have taken the notional income as per the schedule issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority i.e., for the accident of 2015, 8,000/- has to be taken as notional income, wherein the Tribunal has taken the notional income at 7,000/-, which is on the lower side.

sentences.text: The petitioner has produced the wound certificate marked as Ex.P9, which discloses that, she has sustained 4 injuries.

Out of 4 injuries, injury Nos.1 and 2 are simple and injury Nos.3 and 4 are grievous in nature, and the petitioner examined the Doctor as PW4 who has issued the disability certificate marked as Ex.P10, and the Doctor has opined that the petitioner has suffered 40% disability to the whole body,
however, the Tribunal has assessed the disability at 10% to the whole body, which is just and proper.

The petitioner was aged about 35 years as of the date of accident and the petitioner was doing agricultural and animal husbandry works and was earning 15,000/- per month, wherein the Tribunal has taken the notional income at 7,000/- which is on the lower side.
As the accident is of 2015, the Tribunal ought to have taken the notional income at 8,000/-.

The Tribunal, relying - 11 - NC: 2026:KHC-D:3638 HC-KAR upon the evidence of PW4 and the disability certificate at Ex.P10,
the Tribunal has awarded a compensation of 2,06,400/-, which is just and proper.
11. The petitioner is a minor and has sustained fracture of L1 vertebra and fracture of the lower end of the right radius bone.

He was examined by PW4, who has issued the disability certificate at Ex.P18 and has opined that the petitioner has suffered 30% disability to the particular limb, wherein the Tribunal has assessed the disability at 7.5%, which is just and proper, and has rightly awarded a compensation of 1,20,000/-.
12. The impugned common judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is just and proper, and do not call for any interference.
